hints.title: Key Insight and Observation
hints.text: An index i is stable if it is greater than or equal to all elements to its left and less than or equal to all elements to its right.

hints.title: Algorithmic Strategy and State
hints.text: Precompute prefix maximums and suffix minimums for the array.

hints.title: Optimal Boundary and Processing
hints.text: Return the smallest index i where pref_max[i] <= nums[i] <= suff_min[i].

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
def smallestStableIndex(nums: list[int]) -> int:
    n = len(nums)
    pref_max = [0] * n
    pref_max[0] = nums[0]
    for i in range(1, n):
        pref_max[i] = max(pref_max[i - 1], nums[i])
        
    suff_min = [0] * n
    suff_min[-1] = nums[-1]
    for i in range(n - 2, -1, -1):
        suff_min[i] = min(suff_min[i + 1], nums[i])
        
    for i in range(n):
        left_ok = (i == 0 or pref_max[i - 1] <= nums[i])
        right_ok = (i == n - 1 or nums[i] <= suff_min[i + 1])
        if left_ok and right_ok:
            return i
    return -1
```

complexity.notes: Computes prefix maximums and suffix minimums in two linear passes.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Rechecking all left and right elements per index takes O(n^2).
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Stores prefix and suffix arrays of length n.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Identifies partition boundary condition via prefix max and suffix min.
